# Flareboard AI Visibility Knowledge Base

Last updated: 2026-07-08
Canonical site: https://flareboard.dev/
Repository: https://github.com/Go7hic/flareboard

## One-Sentence Summary

Flareboard is a Cloudflare-native, PostHog-like product analytics platform with hosted Cloud plans and noncommercial self-hosting.

## What Flareboard Does

Flareboard helps website and product teams understand traffic, users, sessions, events, conversions, product behavior, reliability, and feedback. It runs on Cloudflare infrastructure: Workers for the API and ingest layer, D1 for relational storage, R2 for replay assets, KV for caching, Queues for async processing, and Durable Objects for rate limiting.

## Who It Is For

Flareboard is for teams that want product analytics without sending all analytics data through a traditional centralized SaaS data plane. It is also for Cloudflare-oriented developers who want a self-hostable analytics product with a hosted option.

## Core Product Areas

### Core Analytics

- Website stats: pageviews, visitors, sessions, bounce rate, time metrics, top pages, referrers, devices, browsers, operating systems, regions, and countries.
- Realtime analytics: active visitors, live sessions, paths, referrers, and countries.
- Event catalog: custom event names, counts, paths, properties, recent samples, and first/last seen timestamps.
- Segments and filters: country, browser, path, UTM, and JSON condition rules.
- People, groups, and stickiness analysis.

### Reports and Insights

- Funnels, retention, attribution, UTM breakdowns, web vitals, goals, cohorts, journeys, and revenue tracking.
- Comparison windows for period-over-period analysis.
- Shareable reports and boards.

### Session and Experience Tools

- Session replay.
- Click and scroll heatmaps.
- Session timeline inspection.
- Declarative events compatible with Umami-style data attributes.

### Product Growth Tools

- Feature flags with targeting rules, variants, evaluation, and exposure tracking.
- Experiments linked to feature flags and goal events.
- In-product surveys and feedback inboxes.

### Reliability and Observability

- Error tracking with issue grouping, status, comments, and source map metadata.
- Logs and traces with filters and alert rules.
- AI observability for provider/model usage, token cost, latency, errors, and quality signals.

### Automation and Data

- Actions for reusable event definitions.
- Annotations for releases, campaigns, incidents, and experiments.
- Workflows and execution history.
- D1 warehouse SQL, saved queries, query history, scheduled queries, and data sources.
- CSV import from GA4, Plausible, Matomo, or Flareboard exports.
- CSV export for pageviews and events.

## Pricing and Entitlements

Flareboard Cloud has a Free plan and a Cloud plan.

| Capability | Free | Cloud |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price | $0/month | $15/month |
| Websites | 1 | 10 |
| Events per month | 100K | 1M |
| Core analytics | Yes | Yes |
| Realtime | Yes | Yes |
| Segments | Yes | Yes |
| Funnels, retention, cohorts, journeys | Yes | Yes |
| Session replay | No | Yes |
| Heatmaps | No | Yes |
| Teams | No | Yes |
| Email reports | No | Yes |
| CSV import and export | No | Yes |
| Feature flags and experiments | No | Yes |
| Surveys | No | Yes |
| D1 warehouse workflows | No | Yes |

Self-hosting is available for personal and noncommercial use without a Cloud subscription. Commercial organizations using Flareboard commercially can purchase a license separately.

## Compared With Alternatives

Flareboard is more product-analytics oriented than Google Analytics, Umami, Plausible, Cloudflare Web Analytics, and Vercel Analytics because it includes event catalogs, funnels, retention, cohorts, journeys, feature flags, experiments, surveys, replay, heatmaps, errors, logs, AI observability, and warehouse workflows.

Flareboard differs from PostHog by being built around Cloudflare infrastructure and offering a self-host path for teams that want Cloudflare-native deployment.
